verdict.root_cause: The frontend's server-side gRPC client for CartService is dialing an endpoint nothing is listening on: from one second after the frontend process started at 01:33:46 it emitted continuous gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE with ECONNREFUSED against 172.18.0.24:7071, persisting unbroken to the end of the window [tr_a88d33972b85]. Cart itself was healthy throughout — zero error ratio with live span metrics [tr_4bb32337d740], uninterrupted ValkeyCartStore info lines with no crash, bind or restart [tr_dd31810e2821], and no recorded deploy, config, flag or restart event [tr_9f256b6d63c3]. Traces place the break on the caller's side: the deepest ERROR span is the frontend's own leaf client span frontend/grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem with no cart-side child, propagating up POST /api/cart to frontend-proxy and load-generator [tr_5fe210eb6383]. A refused connection against a peer that is simultaneously serving other callers is the signature of a wrong destination value in the frontend's CartService configuration, picked up at the 01:33:46 restart, matching the first error-ratio change point at ~01:35Z [tr_1b3d86aa97eb].
verdict.reasoning: ECONNREFUSED is an immediate refusal, not a hang, which excludes process_freeze and network_partition; cart was concurrently serving requests and logging normally [tr_dd31810e2821][tr_4bb32337d740], excluding any cart-side exhaustion, corruption or disk fault. The failing span is the frontend's client span with no downstream child [tr_5fe210eb6383], so the request died at connect. The only way a live, busy service refuses connections on a given address:port is that the caller is dialing an address:port nothing is bound to — the configured value is itself the mechanism. Onset within one second of the frontend restart [tr_a88d33972b85], aligned with the ~01:35Z change point [tr_1b3d86aa97eb], places the fault at configuration load. Fix is to correct the CartService endpoint and restart the frontend. Confidence is medium because no change_history dispatch was run against frontend, so the edit is inferred from behaviour and timing rather than observed.
open_questions: No change_history was queried for frontend; the endpoint edit is inferred, not confirmed by a change record.
What actually listens at 172.18.0.24 and which port cart binds — this separates 'wrong port' from 'stale/wrong host'.
The ~02:22Z second change point and checkout's 02:25 alert are unexplained; checkout also calls cart and was never dispatched on.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart moved to a different container IP and the frontend holds a stale address, so the refusal reflects lost service discovery rather than a wrong authored value.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned caller sees timeouts or no-route, not an immediate refusal from a host that answers; and cart's own log complains about nothing [tr_dd31810e2821].

alternatives.root_cause: A frontend redeploy at 01:33:46 shipped an artifact built against the wrong CartService endpoint.
alternatives.why_not: The logs show a clean start and ready in 344ms with only upstream connection errors [tr_a88d33972b85]; nothing indicates a wrong or unstartable artifact, and no frontend change record was retrieved either way.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no observable effect is predicted. The expected next step is an evidence step, not a remediation one: query change_history for frontend across 2026-10-12T02:24Z..2026-10-13T02:26Z to see whether a prior configuration exists and whether an env/config edit is recorded at or just before the 01:33:46 restart, and resolve what is actually listening on 172.18.0.24 and which port cart binds. If a prior frontend configuration is recorded and names the CartService address, revert_config on frontend becomes proposable and would be confirmed by the ECONNREFUSED 172.18.0.24:7071 lines in {service="frontend"} ceasing and frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR ratio returning toward its 0.00084 baseline.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if change_history for frontend does in fact hold a prior configuration and a config edit inside the window — in that case revert_config's preconditions were met and I withheld a correct fix while the frontend kept failing ~28% of cart requests. It is also wrong if the right fix is purely a dependency-address repair that no recorded prior config can restore, in which case no permitted action addresses the mechanism and the fix is outside this system (reconnect_service and manual endpoint correction are both unavailable).
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible failure of POST /api/cart for the duration, and the unexplained ~02:22Z change point and checkout's 02:25 alert go unaddressed. The risk I am avoiding: revert_config recreates the frontend container and restores a configuration nobody has confirmed exists or differs — if the prior config is identical, the frontend is restarted for nothing (a brief outage with no fix); if the prior config is stale in some other field, it could move frontend's traffic to a different wrong address for ad, recommendation, product-catalog or currency as well as cart. restart_service was also considered and rejected: the evidence points at a destination value, not at process state, and the frontend already started cleanly in 344ms, so a restart would reproduce the same ECONNREFUSED within one second.
proposal.blast_radius: No change is made, so nothing moves. Had revert_config been proposed, it would have touched frontend only, with frontend-proxy and load-generator seeing connection resets during the recreate, and the services frontend's reverted addresses point at — cart, ad, recommendation, product-catalog, currency — seeing traffic shift. checkout, which also calls cart, is unaffected either way and remains undiagnosed.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure spanning frontend, proxy, and checkout with load-generator affected, indicating user-facing breakage rather than a quiet signal. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern doesn't single out a fault class yet.
